extraction.name: RoboFAC dataset
extraction.description: A large-scale and diverse dataset of robotic failure manipulation trajectories and video question-answer (QA) pairs covering robotic tasks of varying complexity across simulation and real-world environments. It comprises 9,440 erroneous manipulation trajectories, 1,282 successful trajectories, and 78,623 QA pairs across 16 tasks, 53 scenes, and six failure taxonomies spanning three hierarchical levels (task planning, motion planning, execution control), labeled across eight question types for task understanding, failure analysis, and failure correction.
extraction.creator: Weifeng Lu, Minghao Ye, Zewei Ye, Ruihan Tao, Shuo Yang, Bo Zhao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Simulation data were collected for 14 robotic tasks in the ManiSkill environment augmented with YCB objects and ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR scenes. Expert policies were defined by target end-effector poses with motion planning, and failure data were generated by replacing the expert policy with code snippets introducing erroneous trajectories/perturbations at selected substages. Real-world data were collected across 6 tasks via teleoperation using the SO-100 robotic arm.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Experiments, Physical data collection, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Recorded robotic manipulation failure and success videos with synchronized viewpoints and accompanying descriptive texts detailing task substages, failure taxonomies, textual error explanations, and perturbed end-effector poses, collected via ManiSkill simulation and real-world SO-100 robotic arm teleoperation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Because motion planning for the robotic arm occasionally failed and caused trajectories not to align with textual descriptions, manual data cleaning was performed, retaining approximately 75% of the collected simulation data.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: QA samples covering eight question types were generated using five randomized question templates per type. Reference answers for five deterministic types (task identification, task planning, failure detection, failure identification, failure locating) were directly extracted from recorded textual descriptions. For the remaining three types (failure explanation, high-level correction, low-level correction), GPT-4o was prompted with the video and descriptive text metadata (task, subtask, error type, error stage, error detail, correction suggestion, perturbation) to generate reference answers, which were subsequently manually reviewed and corrected.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All reference answer outputs generated by GPT-4o for failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction were manually reviewed and corrected by humans to ensure annotation quality.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Integration into VLA-controlled robotic systems is not yet fully seamless or automated; the framework was evaluated exclusively with VLA models rather than direct integration into separate hierarchical planners and controllers; and real-world failure recovery remains bounded by the VLA model's limited ability to follow complex natural language instructions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, evaluating, and benchmarking multimodal large language models and vision-language-action (VLA) models on robotic video understanding, task decomposition, failure analysis (detection, identification, locating, explanation), and failure correction (high-level and low-level recovery).
